confidence_note: Facts from Wikipedia, publisher site and a catalogue blurb; book not read. Only causes named in those sources are used; old text's diet, stress ranking and evolution claims dropped. No case told in detail, so the story is a tour of the causes and the odd examples the book features.
facts: Hari divides the book into 12 deeper causes of the attention crisis.
Among them are physical and mental exhaustion, constant interruption by smartphones, switching between tasks, the decline of mind-wandering, and pollution.
Multitasking is described as ineffective and switching between tasks as wearing down the brain.
Mind-wandering is described as essential for attention to work properly.
The book features veterinarians who diagnose dogs with ADHD.
It features a favela in Rio where everyone lost attention in an unusual way.
It features an office in New Zealand that found a technique to restore workers' attention.
Always-on work culture is argued to cause stress and lower productivity.
tension: A book that starts from phones ends up listing exhaustion, interrupted work, lost daydreaming and pollution too.
opening_idea: Open on the count: twelve causes, and the phone is only one of them.

lessons.idea: When focus fails, look at the whole day and not only at the phone
lessons.anchor: the twelve causes list; Everyday: a bookkeeper who blames her phone for mistakes that appear on the days she slept badly and was interrupted every ten minutes

reflect_final: Which part of your day, other than your phone, takes the most from your focus, and what would you change in it first?

use_cases.situation: A friend blames their phone for everything
use_cases.move: Hari lists twelve causes, and the phone is one. Did you sleep well this week? Interruptions at work?

use_cases.situation: The team asks for a no-phone rule
use_cases.move: Hari counts constant interruption and task switching as causes too. Can we also try one block with no meetings and no chat?

use_cases.situation: You feel unfocused despite a clean screen
use_cases.move: The book says exhaustion and interruptions matter as much. I will go to bed earlier tonight and check my focus tomorrow.

pocket_idea: Hari names twelve causes of lost focus. Before you blame your phone, check the other eleven in your own day.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Hari's list of lost-focus causes has twelve entries, and the phone is only one of them.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Stolen Focus splits the attention crisis into twelve causes, one per chapter. Phones are in there, but so are exhaustion, constant interruptions, the decline of mind-wandering and pollution. The book also visits vets who diagnose dogs with ADHD and an office in New Zealand that found a way to restore attention.
